what_it_does: Modern scientific instruments (electron microscopes, particle detectors, medical imaging systems) generate data faster than local computers can store or analyze. Researchers must decide whether to stream raw data directly to a remote high-performance computing (HPC) center for real-time processing or save it locally first. This paper provides a quantitative framework to guide that decision by measuring trade-offs between transfer time, processing power, and storage I/O costs.
method_in_detail: The framework introduces a Streaming Speed Score metric that combines data generation rate, network transfer efficiency, remote processing power, and local I/O overhead to determine whether streaming or file-based transfer is faster for a given scenario.
